## What the statements say, for zstd
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_halts_may_fail`**: with no memory premise, and even if any request is refused at any point, every execution exits, with any status. Stated for the plain and UBSan builds only.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.
- **`<build>_disagrees_at_most b`**: for inputs drawn from the harness's `Distribution.v`, the plain and sanitizer builds disagree with probability at most *b*.
- **`<build>_agreement_decidable`**: some riscv64 program decides exactly the finite inputs on which the two builds agree. A program that does so, with a bound on how often it rejects, is a route to a disagreement bound (docs/statements.md).

The harnesses with a check whose failure ends the process with a status that a halts statement excludes, so that a proof of that statement implies the check on every input it covers:
- `decompress_cross_format`: one-shot: the same frame decoded as standard zstd1 (magic prepended) and as ZSTD_f_zstd1_magicless must agree on acceptance in both directions, and when both accept, on decompressed size and bytes; streaming: the same comparison with one ZSTD_decompressStream call per format: both return 0 or neither; if both, out.pos equal and output bytes equal.
- `decompress_dstSize_tooSmall`: compress the input at level 1, then decompress into a buffer strictly smaller than the input: must fail, and with exactly ZSTD_error_dstSize_tooSmall (empty input: must return 0).
- `dictionary_loader`: the input is both the dictionary (random load method, content type auto/raw/full, loadDictionary vs refPrefix) and the data: if ZSTD_compress2 succeeds, decompression with the same dictionary must succeed, regenerate the input size and match byte for byte; with ZSTD_dct_rawContent, compression must never fail ("Raw must always succeed!").
- `fse_read_ncount`: FSE_writeNCount must succeed within FSE_NCountWriteBound; build a random valid FSE normalized count (sum = 1<<tableLog), FSE_writeNCount it, append random trailing bytes, FSE_readNCount: must succeed, consume exactly the written size, and return the same maxSymbolValue, tableLog and every count.
- `huf_round_trip`: HIST_count, HUF_buildCTable_wksp and HUF_readDTable must succeed, HUF_optimalTableLog must return <= 12, maxSymbol <= 255; histogram, build and write a Huffman CTable, read it back as a DTable (X1, or X2 falling back to X1), HUF_compress1X/4X then decompress: if compression produced output, decompression must succeed, regenerate the size and match. RLE and incompressible inputs (cSize == 0, or table write failure) are skipped.
- `sequence_compression_api`: random valid sequence list (offsets within the window, optional 1 GiB raw dictionary, explicit or no block delimiters) -> the harness's own decodeSequences builds the source -> ZSTD_compressSequences with validateSequences=1 -> ZSTD_decompressDCtx: must succeed, regenerate the size and match byte for byte.
- `simple_compress`: ZSTD_compressCCtx into a random-size buffer in [0, compressBound]: any failure must be exactly ZSTD_error_dstSize_tooSmall.

## Known issues
None known.

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch zstd
    ./oft verify-sha zstd

By hand: download `zstd-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.10.0](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0), unpack it into `projects/zstd/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; an OSS-Fuzz testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [facebook/zstd](https://github.com/facebook/zstd) at `82d322c4973d9e2968d94047a40892bc6d9a9bdf`, built with CMake
- Harnesses: unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. A binary whose SHA-256 differs after a rebuild with it is a bug: please open an issue.
